contents.name: Exercise 3.9: conjugation action of SU(2) on traceless Hermitian matrices, the homomorphism SU(2) -> SO(3), its surjectivity with kernel {+1,-1}, the universal covering property and pi_1(SO(3)) = Z/2
Section 6.2, Definition 6.6: the quaternion algebra H = R + Ri + Rj + Rk with its multiplication table, the conjugate qbar, the identity q qbar = |q|^2 and the inverse q^{-1} = qbar/|q|^2
Section 6.2: multiplicativity |q_1 q_2| = |q_1| |q_2|, the anti-automorphism property of conjugation, and the division-algebra property
Proposition 6.7: the group of unit quaternions {q : |q| = 1} is isomorphic to SU(2) as a Lie group
Lecture 3, Section 3.3 and the remaining Lie-subgroup and covering-space theory of the notes
contents.reason: The Lie-subgroup machinery and the general covering-space theory of the notes are not promised on this pair: the covering conclusion is taken from the published root example, and the local content is the explicit quaternion differential equation and reconstruction.

contents.name: Introduction Section 1: the linear Lie algebra so(3) = {skew-symmetric real 3-by-3 matrices} of SO(3), equation (0.8)

Section I.8, opening: quaternion conventions, Re xy = Re yx (1.57), conjugation and Re x ybar = Re y xbar (1.58), x xbar = |x|^2
Section I.8, Proposition 1.59 and the classification of the classical matrix Lie algebras over R, C and H
contents.reason: The reductive/semisimple classification of the classical matrix algebras is not promised by this pair; only the section's opening quaternion definitions and identities are read and used.

contents.reason: Interpolation formulae and the document's internal convention catalogue are not promised by this pair; the conventions used here are fixed by the page's own definition of the map rho and the identification phi.

Section 1.4: relationship between quaternion and rotation matrix, orientation of the product, and the small-rotation approximation

contents.reason: The numerical integrators for attitude propagation belong to the report's filtering application and are not part of the double-cover or reconstruction claims promised on this pair.

contents.name: Sections 2.1-2.6: gyro noise model, error-state equation, continuous and discrete error propagation and the state-transition matrix
contents.reason: The Kalman-filter error-state model, its noise assumptions and the discretisation results are engineering applications of the kinematics and are not claimed by this mathematical pair.
